evidence: Caes. BG 1.1: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs
terms.comment: Into parts (in partēs) or among people (inter sē, cum aliquō); Seneca sets the surveyor’s division of a field beside sharing with a brother (Ep. 88.11).
Cicero and Caesar use the deponent; the active partiō is in Plautus and Sallust (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.22: populum in quīnque classēs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs
phrases.english: Gaul as a whole is divided into three parts

phrases.latin: Quid mihi prōdest scīre agellum in partēs dīvidere, sī nesciō cum frātre dīvidere?
phrases.english: What use is it to me to know how to divide a plot of land into parts, if I don’t know how to share it with my brother?

sources: Lewis & Short: divido · Lewis & Short: partio · Lewis & Short: distribuo
